specificities.definition: Inherent and irreducible unpredictability introduced by probabilistic machine learning models, whose outputs are non-deterministic and subject to statistical variance.

indicators.name: non_deterministic_outputs
indicators.description: Results that are not fixed and can vary between runs.

indicators.name: probabilistic_variance
indicators.description: Fluctuations in predictions and estimates based on statistical probability.

indicators.name: model_drift
indicators.description: Performance decay over time due to changing data patterns.

indicators.name: lack_of_reproducibility
indicators.description: The inability to consistently replicate AI-driven results.

indicators.name: data_dependency
indicators.description: High sensitivity to historical data quality and relevance.

indicators.name: non_linear_estimation
indicators.description: Complex relationships in cost and schedule that do not follow traditional linear paths.

indicators.name: opaque_outcomes
indicators.description: Algorithmic decision-making complexities that lead to results that are hard to explain.

indicators.name: dynamic_forecast_adjustment
indicators.description: The need to constantly update baselines as an indicator of underlying system instability.

management_frictions.name: baseline_erosion
management_frictions.description: Probabilistic variance forcing project managers to repeatedly adjust forecasts and commitments.

management_frictions.name: accountability_challenges
management_frictions.description: Opacity in outcomes making it difficult to assign clear responsibility for AI-derived decisions.

specificities.definition: The self-reinforcing, recursive acceleration of AI development that outstrips organizational and human capacity to adapt.

indicators.name: recursive_innovation
indicators.description: AI tools being used to accelerate the development of further AI tools.

indicators.name: skill_obsolescence_pace
indicators.description: Technical and managerial competencies becoming outdated faster than they can be replaced.

indicators.name: judgment_substitution
indicators.description: The reconfiguration of human judgment as AI prediction capabilities improve.

indicators.name: temporal_misalignment
indicators.description: The clash between 'AI time' (fast, iterative) and 'organizational time' (slow, sequential).

indicators.name: regulatory_lag
indicators.description: Governance and ethical frameworks emerging only after technical deployment.

indicators.name: tool_proliferation
indicators.description: New frameworks released faster than they can be systematically evaluated or integrated.

indicators.name: socio_technical_shift
indicators.description: Focus moving from economic benefits to human acceptance and ethics due to technical velocity.

indicators.name: gen_AI_acceleration
indicators.description: Generative AI compounding the rate of change in innovation processes themselves.

management_frictions.name: timeline_compression
management_frictions.description: Rapid tool obsolescence forcing architecture and testing re-evaluations mid-cycle.

management_frictions.name: continuous_training_demand
management_frictions.description: The need for non-stop, modular training to keep up with emerging AI subtypes.

management_frictions.name: integration_debt
management_frictions.description: Managing legacy AI components that are incompatible with new systems or standards.

specificities.definition: Systemic friction emerging when non-linear, data-intensive AI workflows contradict traditional linear, phase-gated processes.

indicators.name: socio_technical_transition
indicators.description: Moving from human-centric to hybrid human-AI collaboration models.

indicators.name: workflow_brittleness
indicators.description: Increased vulnerability in linear processes when integrating adaptive AI.

indicators.name: role_reconfiguration
indicators.description: Project managers shifting toward ethical judgment and system oversight.

indicators.name: integration_friction
indicators.description: Challenges embedding AI into existing phase-based lifecycles (planning, execution, closure).

indicators.name: knowledge_clash
indicators.description: Tension between data-centric AI knowledge and tacit, experience-based human knowledge.

indicators.name: procedural_nonlinearity
indicators.description: Iterative AI loops conflicting with sequential project methodologies.

indicators.name: silo_breakdown
indicators.description: Cross-functional data needs undermining traditional departmental boundaries.

indicators.name: ethical_automation_tension
indicators.description: Conflict between predictive automation and the need for human ethical oversight.

management_frictions.name: legacy_inflexibility
management_frictions.description: Dynamic data needs hindered by legacy software built for static reporting.

management_frictions.name: cultural_resistance
management_frictions.description: Distrust of data-centric approaches in favor of experiential knowledge and waterfall methods.

management_frictions.name: role_transition_hurdles
management_frictions.description: Reskilling needs disrupting established hierarchies and decision-making authority.

specificities.definition: A perceptual gap where stakeholders-driven by hype-view AI as a flawless 'Magic Box'.

indicators.name: dreams_vs_reality
indicators.description: Idealized visions of AI capability contrasted with practical, imperfect outputs.

indicators.name: trust_understanding_gap
indicators.description: High optimism undermined by opaque or unsatisfactory behavior.

indicators.name: paradoxical_expectations
indicators.description: Simultaneous high hopes and high perceived risk toward AI.

indicators.name: magic_box_perception
indicators.description: Belief in AI as an infallible, autonomous solution.

indicators.name: explainability_deficit
indicators.description: Frustration due to lack of transparent, interpretable decision-making.

indicators.name: anthropomorphic_projection
indicators.description: Expecting human-like reasoning or reliability from algorithms.

indicators.name: utility_mismatch
indicators.description: Assuming AI recommendations will perfectly align with personal or organizational goals.

indicators.name: unfairness_barriers
indicators.description: Rejection of AI due to perceived biases or lack of fairness.

management_frictions.name: feedback_dissonance
management_frictions.description: Users providing bug reports based on unrealistic benchmarks, requiring re-education labor.

management_frictions.name: trust_erosion
management_frictions.description: Disillusionment in pilot phases leading to resistance to scaling and demands for redesign.
